Summary: Distance Chart/Cumulative Distance/Maxspeed Chart show validation errors the instant Start Date is clicked, before Generate is ever pressed
Description: Opening Distance Chart (or Cumulative Distance, or Maxspeed Chart) shows a clean form with no errors -- Start Date and End Date both default to the same day via the Yesterday quick-filter. Simply clicking into the Start Date field to open its calendar (no date change, no other field touched, Generate never clicked) immediately triggers the red banner "Start Date and End Date cannot be the same when time selection is not available." three times across the form. The underlying same-day condition was already true before the click; only clicking a field made the pre-existing invalid state visible, consistent with the whole form being marked touched on any field interaction instead of validating on submit. Does not reproduce on Work Hour, Stoppage Summary, Running Summary, or Engine Hour despite those also having Start+End Date pairs, narrowing it to whichever date-range component Distance Chart/Cumulative Distance/Maxspeed Chart share.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and go to Reports > Standard > Distance Chart (or Cumulative Distance, or Maxspeed Chart).
2. Without changing anything, click into the Start Date field to open its calendar picker.
3. Observe the form immediately shows red validation banners, without ever clicking Generate report.
Expected Result: Validation messages should only appear after the user submits invalid data via Generate report, not merely from focusing/opening a date picker.
Actual Result: Three duplicate validation banners appear across the form the instant the Start Date field is clicked, on a form that was valid-looking a moment before and that the user has not actually changed.

Summary: Admin Panel login: backend auth succeeds but the page never redirects to the dashboard after very heavy repeated logins on the same test account
Description: Logging in as the dedicated Admin Panel test account: POST /core/token.php and POST /core/user.php both return 200 with no error, but the page never navigates from the public landing page to /admin/dashboard, hanging 30+ seconds with no error toast or console error. The same flow worked earlier the same day. This surfaced only after the account was used for several hundred rapid, fresh, back-to-back logins in a short window (repeated automated test batch attempts) -- most likely account/session throttling under that volume rather than a defect an ordinary user would hit, but this has not been confirmed either way (no explicit rate-limit or lockout message was shown). Filed as an informational/open observation, not a confirmed-severity bug, pending either a clean retry after time has passed or backend/session-log investigation if it recurs under normal (non-automated) usage.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Have the dedicated Admin Panel test account perform a very large number of fresh logins in a short window (as happened here via repeated automated test runs).
2. Attempt another fresh login as that account via the normal login form.
3. Observe whether the page redirects to /admin/dashboard.
Expected Result: Not applicable / unclear -- this is an open observation, not a confirmed expected-vs-actual defect, since the root cause (throttling vs. a real bug) is not yet established.
Actual Result: Backend login calls return 200 with no error, but the page never redirects to /admin/dashboard and no error is shown to the user.

Summary: AS-219 reconfirmed on production: a Daily scheduled report never arrives by email (checked Inbox and Spam)
Description: Created a genuine Daily-frequency Fleet Summary schedule against a real, checkable inbox, then polled that inbox via IMAP for 6 minutes across both Inbox and Spam folders. No email arrived in either folder. This is the same AS-219 symptom previously confirmed on staging, now reconfirmed on production (v6.trackofy.com). The Spam folder was checked specifically to rule out a delivered-but-filtered false negative. Caveat: only same-day Daily delivery was tested (fire time ~2 minutes after creation) -- if the scheduler is only designed to start firing the day after creation, that would produce this same symptom without being a bug; a next-day delivery check is a reasonable follow-up before treating this as fully conclusive.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and go to Reports > Schedule > New.
2. Create a Daily schedule for Fleet Summary targeting a real, checkable email address, with a near-future delivery time.
3. Wait past the scheduled delivery time and check that email address, including its Spam folder.
Expected Result: The scheduled report email should arrive at the configured address (Inbox or, at minimum, Spam) at or shortly after the scheduled time.
Actual Result: No email arrived in either Inbox or Spam within 6 minutes of the scheduled delivery time.

Summary: Route Management location search (Google Places Autocomplete) returns zero results -- API key not authorized for Places API
Description: Typing into the Origin/Destination/Waypoint search boxes on Create/Edit Route correctly fires real GetPredictions requests to maps.googleapis.com for every keystroke, and every request returns HTTP 200, but the browser console logs: "This API key is not authorized to use this service or API. Please check the API restrictions settings of your API key in the Google Cloud Console...". Confirmed for multiple queries including a single generic character. The base Google Maps JS library and map tiles load fine using the same key -- only the Places Autocomplete predictions service is blocked. Root cause is Google Cloud Console API key configuration (Places API not enabled/authorized for this key), not application code.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Log in and go to Settings > Route Management > Add Route (or Edit an existing route, or Add Waypoint).
2. Type any text into the Origin/Destination/Waypoint location search box.
3. Observe the browser console and whether any location suggestion appears.
Expected Result: Typing a location query should show real Google Places suggestions to pick from.
Actual Result: No suggestions ever appear for any query; the browser console shows a Google API key authorization error for the Places Autocomplete service specifically.
